summary: Recent updates to the image decoding component of Firefox focus on improving the efficiency and reliability of how the browser handles images. By unifying the promise handling (to manage asynchronous tasks), Firefox can now better manage various image types, specifically allowing only specific formats like page-icons and remote images in appropriate contexts. This makes image loading more streamlined. Additionally, technical enhancements such as migrating to `MakeRefPtr` for reference-counted objects and improving the handling of parameters in copy constructs enhance the performance and stability of image operations. Overall, these changes contribute to a smoother browsing experience, _though users may not see any visible change immediately_.
